text:
[LNUL.4.7] **Negated-existence blocks on `null`** (the negation half of "don't
fire on unknown"). [LNUL.4.3] pins the positive case; the **negated-existence**
quantifier must match it, or the silent-wrong-fire this design exists to kill
sneaks back through negation. **A negated-existence pattern `no P where C` is
satisfied iff, for every fact matching `P`, `C` evaluates to `false`.** A fact for
which `C` is `true` (a match) **or** `null` (unknown) **blocks** satisfaction, and
so does a fact for which evaluating `C` raises a fault ([LERR.1.4]): `C` has not
evaluated to `false`, and the fault is recorded as any fault is. So
`no Sensor s where s.state > 85` ("no sensor is hot") does **not** fire while
any sensor's `state` is `null` — you cannot conclude "none hot" while a reading is
unknown. This is the *same* principle as the positive case, not a special one
(**`null` = unknown → don't conclude**, whether the rule asserts presence or
absence); it surfaces as "`null` behaves like `false` positively, like `true`
under negation," but both are one rule. Cost-neutral: the alpha-memory scan
already visits those facts and now tests for `null`-`C` as well as `true`-`C`.
Combines with the pattern-level rule ([LNUL.8.3]).

alloy.name: iret_7_5_1__v5_null_anchor_escapes
alloy.note: WHY THE ANCHOR MUST BE NON-NULL: a null anchor is in no bucket, where the whole `where` is null and blocks the `no` pattern ([LNUL.4.7]).

alloy.name: lnul_4_7__decides
alloy.note: A positive pattern fires on true ([LNUL.4.3]); a `no` pattern is blocked unless false or filtered out, a trap included -- [LNUL.4.7] blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap.

alloy.name: lnul_4_7__pol
alloy.note: A positive pattern, or a `no` pattern.

idris.name: iret_7_6__blocks_join
idris.note: A no node's join relation over the extended token. A trap BLOCKS under `no`. The clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false'), so this proves more than the clause states. The where fragment the Idris model runs produces no trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__blocks
idris.note: A no node is blocked by a candidate unless its tests answer false. A trap BLOCKS under `no`. The clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false'), so this proves more than the clause states. The where fragment the Idris model runs produces no trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__null_comparison_blocks
idris.note: A candidate whose comparison has a null operand blocks, for every operator and every other operand: 'you cannot conclude none hot while a reading is unknown'.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__only_false_passes
idris.note: Only false lets a no pattern pass. A trap BLOCKS under `no`. The clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false'), so this proves more than the clause states. The where fragment the Idris model runs produces no trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__undecided_neither_admits_nor_passes
idris.note: The clause's 'one rule, two sites': an answer that is neither true nor false is not admitted positively and blocks under no. A trap BLOCKS under `no`. The clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false'), so this proves more than the clause states. The where fragment the Idris model runs produces no trap.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__null_anchor_escapes_probe
idris.note: WHY THE CONDITION: a candidate whose anchor answers null blocks under the whole test ([LNUL.4.7]) and is in no bucket -- one blocker against none. The clause is safe because a `linear_scan: false` anchor pins non-null `key` slots; an engine indexing a `no` join on a nullable slot outside `linear_scan: false` must still count the null-keyed candidates, and no clause says so because none specifies that index.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__probe_negated
idris.note: THE PROBE IS TRANSPARENT AT A `no` NODE when the anchor is decided on every candidate: the blockers found in the bucket are exactly the whole list's. Under `linear_scan: false` the condition holds by construction (`iret_7_5_1__typed_anchor_decided`); without it the probe is not transparent (`iret_7_5_1__null_anchor_escapes_probe`).

idris.name: iret_7_6__node_join
idris.note: The relation a node reads from its test: a positive node admits a pair answering true, a `no` node counts a candidate as a blocker unless it answers false. One test, two relations -- RLOW.5.3's 'the same join tests as the positive form'.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__blocks_and_decided
idris.note: A candidate whose first conjunct is decided blocks iff that conjunct holds and the rest blocks -- for any reading of a trap, since the decided conjunct is not one.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__no_blockers_iff_false
idris.note: No candidate blocks a token iff every candidate answers false. A trap BLOCKS under `no`, as Rete/Eval.idr's `lnul_4_7__blocks` has it: the clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false').

idris.name: lnul_4_7__passes_iff_all_false
idris.note: The clause's sentence at the node: a `no` node passes a token it receives iff every candidate of its right memory answers false. A trap BLOCKS under `no`, as Rete/Eval.idr's `lnul_4_7__blocks` has it: the clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false').

idris.name: lnul_4_7__succ_not_zero
idris.note: A count with a blocker in it is not zero.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__v5_probe_negated
idris.note: And at a `no` node when the anchor is decided on every candidate -- hoisting's own condition, carried to `iret_7_5_1__probe_negated`'s by `rlow_5_5__decided_answer`.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__decide
idris.note: The decision: a positive pattern fires on true ([LNUL.4.3]); a `no` pattern is blocked unless false, a trap included -- [LNUL.4.7] blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap, as Rete/NetworkAnswer.idr's `iret_7_6__node_join` has it.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__decide_is_node_join
idris.note: The node's decision is NetworkAnswer's `iret_7_6__node_join` of the V5 test.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__null_filter_differs
idris.note: WHY NON-NULL: a filter answering null rejects the candidate, where the `where` answers null and so blocks a `no` pattern ([LNUL.4.7]).
